source_review.notes: Checked the Dataflow paper and current Apache Beam, Flink, and Spark window, trigger, runner-capability, lateness, and session APIs. All thirteen cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Runtime-specific defaults and feature support are attributed rather than generalized.

evidence: Reviewed event time t, key k, assigner A, width D, slide S, gap G, origin O, rule version v, window state s_k,w, and pane identity P.
Checked fixed/sliding/session intervals are half-open and mathematical floor is distinguished from truncation for negative epochs.
Checked rate lambda, membership m, bytes b, and retention R yield a dimensional byte estimate lambda*m*b*R.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Assignment, trigger action, pane timing/content, allowed lateness, purge, cleanup, and downstream finality use separate terminology.

evidence: Executed fixed-window-trigger-panes with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced assignments (1,0),(4,0),(7,0),(12,10) and panes (0,early,2),(0,on_time,3),(10,on_time,1).
Recomputed one-hour/one-minute maximum membership as 60 and 50,000*60=3,000,000 membership operations/s.
Recomputed Example 3 state as 2,000*900*150=270,000,000 bytes=270 MB decimal.
Recomputed Exercise 2 membership 4 and state 10,000*4*64*30=76,800,000 bytes=76.8 MB decimal.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Arithmetic verifies stated base estimates and local pane behavior only; backend amplification and distributed performance are not measured.

evidence: Verified floor-based fixed assignment selects exactly one n with O+nD<=t<O+(n+1)D.
Checked sliding assignment enumerates every aligned start b satisfying b<=t<b+D and ordinary maximum membership ceil(D/S).
Verified session intervals at 2,10,6 with gap 6 form one connected union [2,16).
Checked cumulative panes 4,9,10 replace to current 10 while discarding deltas 4,5,1 sum to 10 only with deduplicated application.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Trigger correctness is explicitly conditional on trigger state/input progress and does not imply completeness or downstream convergence.

evidence: Reviewed before/at/after interval endpoints, negative epochs, precision rounding, zone folds/gaps, calendar changes, empty/global windows, and timestamp ties.
Reviewed exact watermark/allowed-lateness cleanup boundaries, late bridging sessions, zero/negative/huge gaps, tiny slides, maximum memberships, hot keys, and pane storms.
Reviewed duplicate/reordered input and panes, crash around trigger/sink writes, timer recovery, checkpoint/rescale, and incompatible rule upgrades.
Reviewed producer-controlled configuration, timestamp poisoning, tenant isolation, side-output exposure, retention, and external-effect duplication.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Membership, trigger, state, output, lifecycle, recovery, and security boundaries can fail independently.

evidence: Traced one event through deterministic assignment, keyed window state, trigger update/timer, pane construction, late lifecycle, cleanup, and sink convergence.
Checked every event has exact declared membership and window/pane identities include durable materialization, key, interval/session, result kind, and version semantics.
Checked trigger state/timers, accumulator/content, session merge metadata, and pane versions align with checkpointed input positions.
Checked cleanup occurs only after accepted future events, timers, retries, merges, and corrections no longer need state or reconstruction exists.
invariant_checking.notes: Fire, purge, logical expiration, physical deletion, finality, and external durability remain distinct lifecycle events.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from time domain/assignment through computation, trigger, pane contents, progress, lifecycle, output, capacity/security, and evidence.
Checked half-open fixed coverage proof and deliberate loss of uniqueness for sliding windows.
Checked counterexamples for summing accumulating panes, retrying discarding deltas, and appending late merged sessions.
Checked cleanup proof requires no accepted future dependency or a valid reconstruction path, beyond watermark progress alone.
proof_review.notes: General contracts are separated from Beam, Flink, and Spark-specific APIs/defaults.

evidence: Audited uses of exact, deterministic, bounded, on-time, final, complete, accumulating, discarding, late, purged, and deleted.
Confirmed on-time is relative to watermark behavior and processing-time early panes are labeled provisional/replay-variable.
Confirmed membership amplification, state estimates, session identity, and cleanup claims state premises and exclusions.
Confirmed the fixture disclaims distributed watermarks, lateness, cleanup, recovery, sessions, checkpoints, and sink effects.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No runtime firing or exactly-once operator claim is upgraded into end-to-end completeness or exactly-once external effects.

evidence: Reviewed metrics for assignments/drops, membership, windows/state age/bytes, watermark/fire delay, timer delay, pane classes/versions/retries, merges, late output, cleanup, and sink conflicts.
Reviewed distribution/tail requirements for events/windows per key, raw content, timers, pane churn, correction rate, checkpoint/restore, and freshness.
Confirmed no universal width, slide, gap, trigger period/count, allowed lateness, calendar, accumulator, or sink mode is prescribed.
Confirmed production choices require source distributions, algebra, latency/completeness needs, sink support, failure tests, capacity, policy, and reconciliation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The executable fixture establishes deterministic local semantics, not production capacity, watermark quality, or runtime feature support.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the six separate contracts; fixed/sliding/session/global assignment; trigger state machines; event/processing/count/data/composite triggers; pane accumulation; aggregation state; lateness/cleanup; output identity; recovery; capacity; security; observability; and validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed boundary-safe implementation, calendar versioning, session merge outputs, timer/state bounds, incremental versus buffered aggregation, late reconstruction, sink idempotency, checkpoint/replay, semantic upgrades, quotas, telemetry, and fault injection. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from membership through triggering, pane semantics, lifecycle, and external convergence. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover fixed/sliding/session boundaries, amplification, accumulation, timer delay, lateness, retry, runnable panes, negative epochs, state arithmetic, and production review.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Dataflow/Beam/Flink/Spark maintainer or researcher, distributed-systems/database/data engineer, SRE/performance engineer, calendar/time-zone specialist, security/privacy specialist, sink/tenant owner, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
